findings.reason: the plan makes the storage/loader identity the basis for both the repair target and the load-time refusal, so the wrong operand sends the repair and its check to a matrix the plant never consumes.
findings.text: §7 states "build.py writes linkage.npy only on a sectioned-set miss, and the coil block it splices in is never re-saved. So the build stores the joint matrix it actually uses, coil block included." The two halves contradict. `scripts/iter_sectioned_conductor_set/build.py:258` writes `linkage.npy` from the all-circuit `circuit_linkage_matrix(refined.conductors, circuits, section_n_max=section_n_max)` call, and only afterwards `:287` splices the separate finite-source block (`:276-282`, `finite_source=True`, `section_n_max=6`) into the in-memory `matrix`. The spliced block is therefore exactly the one never re-saved, so the stored file's coil block is NOT the block the build uses. `load_sectioned_machine` (`nova/circuit/passive.py:1193`) reads `matrix = np.load(entry / "linkage.npy")` and sets `section_inductance = matrix[:n_section, :n_section]` with no re-splice, and `coupled_plant` consumes `machine.section_inductance` (`nova/circuit/coupled_plant.py:190`, `:218`), so the delivered plant reads the stored coil block while §7's clause (1) names the finite-source replacement as the quadrature candidate and clause (2) derives "every coil's bare inductance" from the spliced block (`build.py:302`, `coil_matrix = series.T @ matrix[:n_section, :n_section] @ series`). A probe or repair node reasoning from "the stored matrix is the used matrix" would repair the wrong operand, and the loader's new positive-definite check (which reads the file) would not cover the finite-source block the attribution points at.
